source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Hebrew. **THE PRAYER + THE 70 WEEKS PROPHECY**. SECONDARY: 4Q113 (Danielb) preserves fragments of ch 9 — notably 4Q113 frag 16-18 supports several MT readings against OG. TERTIARY: OG-Greek + Theodotion-Greek consulted at the calendrical cruxes of vv 24-27. The OG of 9:24-27 differs substantially from MT in the structuring of the 'weeks' divisions; Theodotion conforms more closely to MT.
source.transliteration_convention: SBL Hebrew convention throughout (Tiberian vocalization per Codex Leningradensis).
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999; Jubilees per VanderKam DJD XIII.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 9 — HEBREW, Daniel's prayer + Gabriel's 70-weeks oracle. **TWO PARTS**: (i) vv 1-19 — Daniel's penitential prayer over the 70-years-of-Jeremiah (Jer 25:11, 29:10); modeled on Deuteronomistic confessional prayers (cf. 1 Kgs 8; Ezra 9; Neh 9; Bar 1:15-3:8). (ii) vv 20-27 — Gabriel's appearance and the 70-weeks-of-years oracle (9:24-27), one of the most contested calendrical-messianic prophecies in scripture. **CROSS-CORPUS DENSITY**: the 70-weeks (490 years) directly informs Jubilees' jubilee-chronology (10 × 49 years = 490); the Qumran *Apocalypse of Weeks* (1 En 93 + 91:11-17); the *Animal Apocalypse* (1 En 85-90); 11QMelchizedek; the rabbinic chronology of Seder Olam Rabbah ch 28-30; the patristic Christian readings (Eusebius, Africanus); and the entire dispensationalist tradition. The 'abomination of desolation' (v 27) is the most-quoted Daniel phrase in the NT (Matt 24:15, Mark 13:14).

verses.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְדָרְיָ֛וֶשׁ בֶּן־אֲחַשְׁוֵר֖וֹשׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָמְלַ֔ךְ עַ֖ל מַלְכ֥וּת כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
verses.translit: bi-šnaṯ ʾaḥaṯ lə-Dāryāweš ben-ʾĂḥašwērōš miz-zeraʿ Māḏāy ʾăšer hāmlaḵ ʿal malḵūṯ Kaśdîm
verses.notes: **In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, by birth a Mede, who became king over the realm of the Chaldeans...** **CHRONOLOGICAL FRAMING**: 'first year of Darius the Mede' = the Persian conquest of Babylon's first year, c. 539 BCE. **HISTORICAL NOTE**: 'Ahasuerus' (אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ ʾĂḥašwērōš) here as Darius's *father* — historically problematic (Ahasuerus = Xerxes I, who was Darius I's *son*, not father). The Daniel-figure 'Darius the Mede' is literary-theological, not strictly historical (see ch 6:1 note).

verses.text: בִּשְׁנַ֤ת אַחַת֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ אֲנִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בִּינֹ֖תִי בַּסְּפָרִ֑ים מִסְפַּ֣ר הַשָּׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יִרְמִיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא לְמַלֹּ֛אות לְחָרְב֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
verses.translit: bi-šnaṯ ʾaḥaṯ lə-mālḵō ʾănî Dāniyyēʾl bînōṯî bas-səp̄ārîm mispar haš-šānîm ʾăšer hāyāh ḏəḇar-Yhwh ʾel-Yirmiyāh han-nāḇîʾ lə-mallōʾṯ lə-ḥorḇōṯ Yərūšālaim šiḇʿîm šānāh
verses.notes: **...in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, perceived in the books the number of years which, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, must pass before the end of the desolations of Jerusalem, namely, seventy years.** **THE 70 YEARS OF JEREMIAH** — cross-reference to Jer 25:11-12 + 29:10. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: this verse is the foundational instance of intra-canonical interpretive practice — Daniel READS scripture (Jeremiah) and re-interprets it through angelic mediation. The 70-years-of-exile (587-538 BCE per Persian-period chronology; or 605-538 BCE per Jeremiah's count from the first deportation) is re-interpreted in vv 24-27 as 70 weeks-of-years (490 years). cf. 2 Chr 36:21 (the seventy years connected to sabbatical-rest); cf. Zech 1:12, 7:5. cf. Jub 1:29 (the jubilee-chronology framework). cf. 1 En 89:59 — the Animal Apocalypse's '70 shepherds' is a parallel reinterpretation of the 70-years. **THE 'BOOKS'** (בַּסְּפָרִים bas-səp̄ārîm) implies Daniel had access to a collection of prophetic writings — early canon-formation evidence.

verses.text: וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה אֶת־פָּנַ֗י אֶל־אֲדֹנָי֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ תְּפִלָּ֖ה וְתַחֲנוּנִ֑ים בְּצ֖וֹם וְשַׂ֥ק וָאֵֽפֶר׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾettənāh ʾeṯ-pānay ʾel-ʾĂḏōnāy hā-ʾĔlōhîm lə-ḇaqqēš təp̄illāh wə-ṯaḥănūnîm bə-ṣōm wə-śaq wā-ʾēp̄er
verses.notes: **Then I turned my face to the Lord God, seeking him by prayer and supplications with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.** **THE PENITENTIAL TRIAD**: fasting + sackcloth + ashes — standard Israelite penitential praxis. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Joel 2:12-13; Esth 4:1-3; Neh 9:1; Jonah 3:5-8; cf. Matt 11:21 / Luke 10:13 (Jesus invokes 'sackcloth and ashes'). The third Daniel-prayer (besides 6:11).

verses.text: וָֽאֶתְפַּֽלְלָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י וָאֶתְוַדֶּ֑ה וָאֹמְרָ֗ה אָנָּ֤א אֲדֹנָי֙ הָאֵ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾeṯpalləlāh la-Yhwh ʾĔlōhay wā-ʾeṯwaddeh wā-ʾōmərāh ʾānnāʾ ʾĂḏōnāy hā-ʾĒl hag-gāḏōl wə-han-nōrāʾ šōmēr hab-bərîṯ wə-ha-ḥeseḏ lə-ʾōhăḇāyw ū-lə-šōmərê miṣwōṯāyw
verses.notes: **I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession, saying: 'O Lord, the great and terrible God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments...'** **OPENING FORMULA** parallels Deut 7:9, 10:17, Neh 1:5 — Deuteronomistic confessional convention. **NOTE**: this is one of the FEW occurrences of the divine name YHWH (יהוה) in the book of Daniel — appears in 9:2, 9:4, 9:10, 9:13, 9:14, 9:20. The rest of Daniel uses אֱלֹהִים, אֲדֹנָי, or Aramaic אֱלָהָא.

verses.text: חָטָ֥אנוּ וְעָוִ֖ינוּ והרשענו וְהִרְשַׁ֣עְנוּ וּמָרָ֑דְנוּ וְס֥וֹר מִמִּצְוֺתֶ֖ךָ וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃
verses.translit: ḥāṭāʾnū wə-ʿāwînū wə-hiršaʿnū ū-mārāḏnū wə-sōr mim-miṣwōṯeḵā ū-mim-mišpāṭêḵā
verses.notes: **'...we have sinned and done wrong and acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and ordinances.'** **FOURFOLD CONFESSION-VOCABULARY**: ḥāṭāʾ + ʿāwāh + rāšaʿ + mārāḏ — exhausts the Hebrew sin-vocabulary. **CROSS-CORPUS**: pattern echoed in 1 Kgs 8:47; Ps 106:6; Bar 2:12. Qere-ketiv: והרשענו/וְהִרְשַׁעְנוּ.

verses.text: וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבְּרוּ֙ בְּשִׁמְךָ֔ אֶל־מְלָכֵ֥ינוּ שָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
verses.translit: wə-lōʾ šāmaʿnū ʾel-ʿăḇāḏêḵā han-nəḇîʾîm ʾăšer dibbərū bə-šimḵā ʾel-məlāḵênū śārênū wa-ʾăḇōṯênū wə-ʾel kol-ʿam hā-ʾāreṣ
verses.notes: **'We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.'**

verses.text: לְךָ֤ אֲדֹנָי֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה וְלָ֛נוּ בֹּ֥שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֖ים כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וּלְיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּֽלְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים וְהָרְחֹקִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם בְּמַעֲלָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעֲלוּ־בָֽךְ׃
verses.translit: lə-ḵā ʾĂḏōnāy haṣ-ṣəḏāqāh wə-lānū bōšeṯ hap-pānîm kay-yōm haz-zeh lə-ʾîš Yəhūḏāh ū-lə-yōšəḇê Yərūšālaim ū-lə-ḵol-Yiśrāʾēl haq-qərōḇîm wə-hā-rəḥōqîm bə-ḵol-hā-ʾărāṣōṯ ʾăšer hiddaḥtām šām bə-maʿălām ʾăšer māʿălū-ḇāḵ
verses.notes: **'To you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us confusion of face, as at this day, to the people of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those that are near and those that are far away, in all the lands to which you have driven them, because of the treachery which they have committed against you.'**

verses.text: יְהוָ֗ה לָ֚נוּ בֹּ֣שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֔ים לִמְלָכֵ֥ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃
verses.translit: Yhwh lānū bōšeṯ hap-pānîm li-mlāḵênū lə-śārênū wə-la-ʾăḇōṯênū ʾăšer ḥāṭāʾnū lāḵ
verses.notes: **'O LORD, to us belongs confusion of face, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against you.'**

verses.text: לַֽאדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הָרַחֲמִ֖ים וְהַסְּלִח֑וֹת כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְנוּ בּֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: la-ʾḎōnāy ʾĔlōhênū hā-raḥămîm wə-has-səliḥōṯ kî māraḏnū bō
verses.notes: **'To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness; for we have rebelled against him.'** **TERM**: סְלִיחוֹת (səlîḥōṯ 'forgivenesses') — plural — the noun-form underlies the rabbinic *Selichot* penitential-prayer tradition (recited before Rosh Hashanah).

verses.text: וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לָלֶ֤כֶת בְּתֽוֹרֹתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣ן לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
verses.translit: wə-lōʾ šāmaʿnū bə-qōl Yhwh ʾĔlōhênū lā-leḵeṯ bə-ṯōrōṯāyw ʾăšer nāṯan lə-p̄ānênū bə-yaḏ ʿăḇāḏāyw han-nəḇîʾîm
verses.notes: **'We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God by following his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.'**

verses.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עָֽבְרוּ֙ אֶת־תּ֣וֹרָתֶ֔ךָ וְס֕וֹר לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּקֹלֶ֑ךָ וַתִּתַּ֨ךְ עָלֵ֜ינוּ הָאָלָ֣ה וְהַשְּׁבֻעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כְּתוּבָה֙ בְּתוֹרַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-ḵol-Yiśrāʾēl ʿāḇərū ʾeṯ-tōrāṯeḵā wə-sōr lə-ḇiltî šəmōaʿ bə-qōleḵā wat-tittaḵ ʿālênū hā-ʾālāh wə-haš-šəḇuʿāh ʾăšer kəṯūḇāh bə-ṯōraṯ Mōšeh ʿeḇeḏ-hā-ʾĔlōhîm kî ḥāṭāʾnū lō
verses.notes: **'All Israel has transgressed your law and turned aside, refusing to obey your voice; and the curse and oath which are written in the Law of Moses the servant of God have been poured out upon us, because we have sinned against him.'** **'CURSE AND OATH'** — the Deuteronomic-covenant maledictions (Deut 28:15-68; 29:18-28; Lev 26:14-39).

verses.text: וַיָּ֜קֶם אֶת־דבריו דְּבָר֣וֹ ׀ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלֵ֗ינוּ וְעַ֤ל שֹֽׁפְטֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁפָט֔וּנוּ לְהָבִ֥יא עָלֵ֖ינוּ רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־נֶעֶשְׂתָ֗ה תַּ֚חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.translit: way-yāqem ʾeṯ-dəḇārō ʾăšer-dibber ʿālênū wə-ʿal šōp̄əṭênū ʾăšer šəp̄āṭūnū lə-hāḇîʾ ʿālênū rāʿāh ḡəḏōlāh ʾăšer lōʾ-neʿeśtāh taḥaṯ kol-haš-šāmayim ka-ʾăšer neʿeśtāh bî-Rūšālāim
verses.notes: **'He has confirmed his words, which he spoke against us and against our rulers who ruled us, by bringing upon us a great calamity; for under the whole heaven there has not been done the like of what has been done against Jerusalem.'** **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Lam 1:12; 2:13 — the unique-suffering-of-Jerusalem topos. Qere-ketiv: דבריו/דְּבָרוֹ.

verses.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בָּ֣אָה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹֽא־חִלִּ֜ינוּ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לָשׁוּב֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וּלְהַשְׂכִּ֖יל בַּאֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
verses.translit: ka-ʾăšer kāṯūḇ bə-ṯōraṯ Mōšeh ʾēṯ kol-hā-rāʿāh haz-zōʾṯ bāʾāh ʿālênū wə-lōʾ-ḥillînū ʾeṯ-pənê Yhwh ʾĔlōhênū lā-šūḇ mē-ʿăwōnēnū ū-lə-haśkîl ba-ʾămiteḵā
verses.notes: **'As it is written in the Law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us, yet we have not entreated the favor of the LORD our God, turning from our iniquities and giving heed to your truth.'**

verses.text: וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַיְבִיאֶ֖הָ עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־צַדִּ֞יק יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עַל־כָּל־מַֽעֲשָׂיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: way-yišqōḏ Yhwh ʿal-hā-rāʿāh way-ḇîʾehā ʿālênū kî-ṣaddîq Yhwh ʾĔlōhênū ʿal-kol-maʿăśāyw ʾăšer ʿāśāh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿnū bə-qōlō
verses.notes: **'Therefore the LORD has kept ready the calamity and has brought it upon us; for the LORD our God is righteous in all the works which he has done, and we have not obeyed his voice.'** **TERM**: שָׁקַד (šāqaḏ 'to watch / keep ready') — wordplay on Jer 1:11-12 (the *shaqed* almond-rod + *shoqed* watching). Daniel's prayer cites Jeremiah at vocabulary-level.

verses.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ הוֹצֵ֨אתָ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֜ מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה וַתַּֽעַשׂ־לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿattāh ʾĂḏōnāy ʾĔlōhênū ʾăšer hōṣēʾṯā ʾeṯ-ʿammə-ḵā mē-ʾereṣ Miṣrayim bə-yāḏ ḥăzāqāh wat-taʿaś-lə-ḵā šēm kay-yōm haz-zeh ḥāṭāʾnū rāšāʿnū
verses.notes: **'And now, O Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and have made yourself a name, as at this day — we have sinned, we have done wickedly.'** **THE EXODUS-INVOCATION** as ground of petition — standard Israelite confessional move.

verses.text: אֲדֹנָ֗י כְּכָל־צִדְקֹתֶ֙ךָ֙ יָֽשָׁב־נָ֤א אַפְּךָ֙ וַחֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ מֵעִֽירְךָ֥ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הַר־קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֤י בַחֲטָאֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּבַעֲוֺנ֣וֹת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֧ם וְעַמְּךָ֛ לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לְכָל־סְבִיבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
verses.translit: ʾĂḏōnāy kə-ḵol-ṣiḏqōṯeḵā yāšāḇ-nāʾ ʾappə-ḵā wa-ḥămāṯə-ḵā mē-ʿîrə-ḵā Yərūšālaim har-qoḏšeḵā kî ḇa-ḥăṭāʾênū ū-ḇa-ʿăwōnōṯ ʾăḇōṯênū Yərūšālaim wə-ʿammə-ḵā lə-ḥerpāh lə-ḵol-səḇîḇōṯênū
verses.notes: **'O Lord, according to all your righteous acts, let your anger and your wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy hill; because for our sins, and for the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people have become a byword among all who are around us.'**

verses.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ שְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאֶל־תַּ֣חֲנוּנָ֔יו וְהָאֵ֣ר פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־מִקְדָּשְׁךָ֖ הַשָּׁמֵ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן אֲדֹנָֽי׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿattāh šəmaʿ ʾĔlōhênū ʾel-təp̄illaṯ ʿaḇdə-ḵā wə-ʾel-taḥănūnāyw wə-hāʾēr pāneḵā ʿal-miqdāšə-ḵā haš-šāmēm lə-maʿan ʾĂḏōnāy
verses.notes: **'Now therefore, O our God, hearken to the prayer of your servant, and to his supplications, and for your own sake, O Lord, cause your face to shine upon your desolated sanctuary.'** **TERM**: הָאֵר פָּנֶיךָ (hāʾēr pāneḵā 'cause your face to shine') — quotation of the Aaronic Blessing (Num 6:25).

verses.text: הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י ׀ אָזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשֲׁמָע֒ פקחה פְּקַ֣ח עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א עַל־צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃
verses.translit: haṭṭēh ʾĔlōhay ʾoznə-ḵā ū-šămāʿ pəqaḥ ʿêneḵā ū-rəʾēh šōmə-mōṯênū wə-hā-ʿîr ʾăšer-niqrāʾ šim-ḵā ʿāleyhā kî lōʾ ʿal-ṣiḏqōṯênū ʾănaḥnū mappîlîm taḥănūnênū lə-p̄āneḵā kî ʿal-raḥămeḵā hā-rabbîm
verses.notes: **'O my God, incline your ear and hear; open your eyes and see our desolations, and the city which is called by your name; for we do not present our supplications before you on the ground of our righteousness, but on the ground of your great mercy.'** Qere-ketiv: פקחה/פְּקַח.

verses.text: אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ שְׁמָ֙עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י ׀ סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקֲשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעֲנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־עַמֶּֽךָ׃
verses.translit: ʾĂḏōnāy šəmāʿāh ʾĂḏōnāy səlāḥāh ʾĂḏōnāy haqăšîḇāh wa-ʿăśēh ʾal-təʾaḥar lə-maʿan-ḵā ʾĔlōhay kî-šim-ḵā niqrāʾ ʿal-ʿîrə-ḵā wə-ʿal-ʿammeḵā
verses.notes: **'O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, give heed and act; delay not, for your own sake, O my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.'** **THE PRAYER'S CRESCENDO**: triple ʾĂḏōnāy — hear/forgive/act. cf. 1 Kgs 8:30 (Solomon's prayer) — same triadic petitionary form.

verses.text: וְע֨וֹד אֲנִ֤י מְדַבֵּר֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וּמִתְוַדֶּה֙ חַטָּאתִ֔י וְחַטַּ֖את עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַפִּ֣יל תְּחִנָּתִ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י עַ֖ל הַר־קֹ֥דֶשׁ אֱלֹהָֽי׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿōḏ ʾănî mə-ḏabbēr ū-miṯpallēl ū-miṯwaddeh ḥaṭṭāʾṯî wə-ḥaṭṭaʾṯ ʿammî Yiśrāʾēl ū-mappîl təḥinnāṯî lip̄nê Yhwh ʾĔlōhay ʿal har-qōḏeš ʾĔlōhāy
verses.notes: **While I was speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God for the holy hill of my God...** Transition from prayer (vv 4-19) to Gabriel's response (vv 21-27).

verses.text: וְע֛וֹד אֲנִ֥י מְדַבֵּ֖ר בַּתְּפִלָּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ רָאִ֨יתִי בֶחָז֤וֹן בַּתְּחִלָּה֙ מֻעָ֣ף בִּיעָ֔ף נֹגֵ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י כְּעֵ֖ת מִנְחַת־עָֽרֶב׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿōḏ ʾănî mə-ḏabbēr bat-təp̄illāh wə-hā-ʾîš Gaḇrîʾēl ʾăšer rāʾîṯî ḇe-ḥāzōn bat-təḥillāh muʿāp̄ bî-ʿāp̄ nōḡēaʿ ʾēlay kə-ʿēṯ minḥaṯ-ʿāreḇ
verses.notes: **...while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the first, came to me in swift flight at the time of the evening sacrifice.** **GABRIEL'S RETURN** (cf. 8:16). **'AT THE TIME OF THE EVENING SACRIFICE'** (כְּעֵת מִנְחַת־עָרֶב) — c. 3 PM, the *minḥah* offering. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Luke 1:10-11 (Gabriel appears to Zechariah 'at the hour of incense', a related daily offering); cf. Acts 3:1 (Peter and John go to the temple at 'the ninth hour, the hour of prayer'). The Daniel-Gabriel-at-the-minchah pattern directly shapes Luke 1:10.

verses.text: וַיָּ֖בֶן וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמִּ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר דָּנִיֵּ֕אל עַתָּ֥ה יָצָ֖אתִי לְהַשְׂכִּילְךָ֥ בִינָֽה׃
verses.translit: way-yāḇen way-ḏabbēr ʿimmî way-yōmar Dāniyyēʾl ʿattāh yāṣāʾṯî lə-haśkîl-ḵā ḇînāh
verses.notes: **He made me understand, speaking with me, and saying: 'O Daniel, I have now come out to give you wisdom and understanding.'**

verses.text: בִּתְחִלַּ֨ת תַּחֲנוּנֶ֜יךָ יָצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר וַאֲנִי֙ בָּ֣אתִי לְהַגִּ֔יד כִּ֥י חֲמוּד֖וֹת אָ֑תָּה וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
verses.translit: bi-ṯḥillaṯ taḥănūneḵā yāṣāʾ ḏāḇār wa-ʾănî bāʾṯî lə-haggîḏ kî ḥămūḏōṯ ʾāttāh ū-ḇîn bad-dāḇār wə-hāḇēn bam-marʾeh
verses.notes: **'At the beginning of your supplications a word went forth, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are greatly beloved; therefore consider the word and understand the vision.'** **'GREATLY BELOVED'** (חֲמוּדוֹת ḥămūḏōṯ — lit. 'desirable things / preciousness') — Daniel's epithet, reappears in 10:11, 10:19. The OG/Theodotion ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν 'man of desires/longings'. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mark 1:11 / Matt 3:17 ('this is my beloved son'); cf. Eph 1:6 ('the Beloved' as title).

verses.text: שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־עַמְּךָ֣ ׀ וְעַל־עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע ולחתם וּלְהָתֵ֤ם חטאות חַטָּאת֙ וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֺ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָז֣וֹן וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃
verses.translit: šāḇuʿîm šiḇʿîm neḥtaḵ ʿal-ʿammə-ḵā wə-ʿal-ʿîr qoḏšeḵā lə-ḵallēʾ hap-pešaʿ ū-lə-hāṯēm ḥaṭṭāʾṯ ū-lə-ḵappēr ʿāwōn ū-lə-hāḇîʾ ṣeḏeq ʿōlāmîm wə-laḥtōm ḥāzōn wə-nāḇîʾ wə-li-mšōaḥ qōḏeš qāḏāšîm
verses.witness_tertiary: OG-Greek: ἑβδομήκοντα ἑβδομάδες; Theodotion likewise. Both versions translate 'seventy weeks' = 70 sabbatical periods.
verses.notes: **'Seventy weeks of years are decreed concerning your people and your holy city, to finish the transgression, to put an end to sin, and to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal both vision and prophet, and to anoint a most holy place.'** **THE 70 WEEKS OF YEARS — MAJOR CALENDRICAL-MESSIANIC PROPHECY**. **TERMS**: שָׁבֻעִים שִׁבְעִים (šāḇuʿîm šiḇʿîm) literally 'seventy sevens / heptads' — read as 70 sabbatical-year cycles = 70 × 7 years = **490 YEARS**. **SIX PURPOSES**: (1) finish transgression, (2) end sin, (3) atone iniquity, (4) bring everlasting righteousness, (5) seal vision and prophet, (6) anoint a most holy. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: (a) **JUBILEES CHRONOLOGY**: Jubilees' 49-year jubilee × 10 = 490, structurally identical to Daniel's 70 × 7 = 490; Jub 50 explicitly closes the chronology at 49 jubilees (= 2401 years from creation to entry into Canaan). The 490-year framework underlies both texts. (b) **APOCALYPSE OF WEEKS (1 En 93 + 91:11-17)**: ten 'weeks' of history — Enochic parallel to Daniel's 70-week scheme. (c) **11QMELCHIZEDEK** (11Q13): explicitly cites Dan 9:24-27 within a jubilee-of-jubilees framework; Melchizedek brings the eschatological *kippur* (atonement). (d) **SEDER OLAM RABBAH ch 28-30**: the rabbinic chronology calculates the 490 years from the destruction of the First Temple (587 BCE) to the destruction of the Second Temple (70 CE) — a major rabbinic harmonization that historicizes the prophecy as fulfilled in 70 CE. (e) **CHRISTIAN/PATRISTIC**: Eusebius (Demonstratio Evangelica 8.2), Julius Africanus, Hippolytus — all calculate the 490 years as terminating with the death/resurrection of Christ. (f) **DISPENSATIONALIST**: J.N. Darby + Scofield — the 70th week is parenthetically separated as future. **'TO ANOINT A MOST HOLY'** (לִמְשֹׁחַ קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים li-mšōaḥ qōḏeš qāḏāšîm) — either the temple's Holy of Holies, or a messianic anointing (the 'most holy one'). Qere-ketiv: ולחתם/וּלְהָתֵם; חטאות/חַטָּאת. Cross-reference to 9:24-27 (70 weeks-of-years calendrical numerology); see also 9:27 (abomination of desolation).

verses.text: וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל מִן־מֹצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר לְהָשִׁיב֙ וְלִבְנ֤וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עַד־מָשִׁ֣יחַ נָגִ֔יד שָׁבֻעִ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְשָׁבֻעִ֞ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֗יִם תָּשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנְתָה֙ רְח֣וֹב וְחָר֔וּץ וּבְצ֖וֹק הָעִתִּֽים׃
verses.translit: wə-ṯēḏaʿ wə-ṯaśkēl min-mōṣāʾ ḏāḇār lə-hāšîḇ wə-li-ḇnōṯ Yərūšālaim ʿaḏ-māšîaḥ nāḡîḏ šāḇuʿîm šiḇʿāh wə-šāḇuʿîm šiššîm ū-šənayim tāšūḇ wə-niḇnəṯāh rəḥōḇ wə-ḥārūṣ ū-ḇə-ṣōq hā-ʿittîm
verses.notes: **'Know therefore and understand that from the going forth of the word to restore and build Jerusalem to the coming of an anointed one, a prince, there shall be seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it shall be built again with squares and moat, but in a troubled time.'** **THE TIMETABLE — STRUCTURED IN UNITS OF SEVEN**: (a) 7 weeks (49 years) from 'the word' to the 'anointed prince'; (b) + 62 weeks (434 years) of rebuilding; (c) + 1 week (7 years; v 27) — total 70 weeks = 490 years. **'THE GOING FORTH OF THE WORD' — FOUR PROPOSED START-POINTS**: (i) Jeremiah's prophecy c. 605 BCE; (ii) Cyrus's decree 538 BCE (per Ezra 1); (iii) Artaxerxes' decree to Ezra 458 BCE; (iv) Artaxerxes' decree to Nehemiah 445 BCE. **'AN ANOINTED ONE, A PRINCE'** (מָשִׁיחַ נָגִיד māšîaḥ nāḡîḏ): scholarly debate — (a) Cyrus (Isa 45:1 calls Cyrus *māšîaḥ*); (b) Joshua the high priest (Zech 3); (c) Onias III (high priest murdered 171 BCE, per 2 Macc 4:34); (d) Jesus Christ (Christian reading). Critical reading (Collins, Newsom, Hartman-DiLella): the 7-week period ends with Joshua/Zerubbabel; the 62-week period ends with Onias III's death; the 70th week is Antiochus IV's persecution. **NOTE ON PUNCTUATION**: MT vowel-points place the *atnach* (major pause) after 'seven weeks', linking 'seven weeks' to the anointed-prince and the '62 weeks' to the rebuilding-period; some Christian translations (KJV, NIV) repunctuate to read '7+62 = 69 weeks to Messiah'. The MT pointing is the older reading.

verses.text: וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַשָּׁבֻעִים֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֔יִם יִכָּרֵ֥ת מָשִׁ֖יחַ וְאֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ וְהָעִ֨יר וְהַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יַ֠שְׁחִית עַ֣ם נָגִ֤יד הַבָּא֙ וְקִצּ֣וֹ בַשֶּׁ֔טֶף וְעַד֙ קֵ֣ץ מִלְחָמָ֔ה נֶחֱרֶ֖צֶת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾaḥărê haš-šāḇuʿîm šiššîm ū-šənayim yikkārēṯ māšîaḥ wə-ʾên lō wə-hā-ʿîr wə-haq-qōḏeš yašḥîṯ ʿam nāḡîḏ hab-bāʾ wə-qiṣṣō ḇaš-šeṭep̄ wə-ʿaḏ qēṣ milḥāmāh neḥĕreṣeṯ šōmēmōṯ
verses.notes: **'And after the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one shall be cut off, and shall have nothing; and the people of the prince who is to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end shall come with a flood, and to the end there shall be war; desolations are decreed.'** **THE CUTTING-OFF OF THE ANOINTED**: **CRITICAL READING** (Collins): Onias III's murder in 171 BCE (cf. 2 Macc 4:33-34); 'the people of the prince' = Antiochus IV's forces who profaned the Temple in 167 BCE (cf. 1 Macc 1:20-64). **CHRISTIAN READING**: the anointed = Jesus crucified c. 30/33 CE; the prince = Titus who destroyed Jerusalem 70 CE. **'CUT OFF AND HAS NOTHING'** (יִכָּרֵת מָשִׁיחַ וְאֵין לוֹ yikkārēṯ māšîaḥ wə-ʾên lō): **CROSS-CORPUS** cf. Isa 53:8 ('cut off from the land of the living') — the suffering-servant parallel is striking; cf. Mark 15:34 ('My God, my God, why have you forsaken me'). The phrase is the foundational Christian Christological proof-text. **'THE PRINCE WHO IS TO COME'** is foundationally identified in dispensationalism with Antichrist.

verses.text: וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד וַחֲצִ֨י הַשָּׁב֜וּעַ יַשְׁבִּ֣ית ׀ זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְעַ֨ל כְּנַ֤ף שִׁקּוּצִים֙ מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם וְעַד־כָּלָה֙ וְנֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה תִּתַּ֖ךְ עַל־שֹׁמֵֽם׃
verses.translit: wə-hiḡbîr bərîṯ lā-rabbîm šāḇūaʿ ʾeḥāḏ wa-ḥăṣî haš-šāḇūaʿ yašbîṯ zeḇaḥ ū-minḥāh wə-ʿal kənap̄ šiqqūṣîm məšōmēm wə-ʿaḏ-kālāh wə-neḥĕrāṣāh tittaḵ ʿal-šōmēm
verses.witness_tertiary: OG: 'on the temple [shall be] an abomination of desolations'; Theodotion: 'on the temple [shall be] an abomination of desolation' (singular). The Theodotion τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως is the form quoted in Matt 24:15 + Mark 13:14.
verses.notes: **'And he shall make a strong covenant with many for one week; and for half of the week he shall cause sacrifice and offering to cease; and upon the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate, until the decreed end is poured out on the desolator.'** **THE 70TH WEEK + THE ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION — MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS NODE**. **'THE ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION'** (שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם šiqqūṣîm məšōmēm) — appears here, 11:31, 12:11. **CRITICAL READING**: Antiochus IV's altar to Olympian Zeus erected on the Jerusalem altar 15 Kislev 167 BCE (1 Macc 1:54; 2 Macc 6:2). The Aramaic *šiqqūṣ* puns on the Aramaic-Greek *Baʿal Šāmēm* / *Zeus Ouranios* — the substitute deity. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR NT**: (a) **Matt 24:15 + Mark 13:14**: 'when you see the desolating sacrilege (τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως) spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place — let the reader understand —' — DIRECT QUOTATION of Dan 9:27 / 11:31. The Olivet discourse explicitly cites Daniel. (b) **2 Thess 2:3-4**: 'the man of lawlessness... takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God' — direct Dan 9:27 + 11:36-37 inheritance. (c) **Rev 13:14-15**: the image of the beast set up in the temple. (d) **1 Macc 1:54**: 'set up an abominable thing of desolation upon the altar' — verbatim citation. **HALF-A-WEEK = 3.5 YEARS**: corresponds to the Antiochene persecution-duration (December 167 BCE to December 164 BCE / Hanukkah). Same numeric pattern as 7:25 ('time, times, half a time') + 12:7. Cross-reference to 9:24-27 calendrical numerology + cross-corpus to Mt 24:15 + Mk 13:14 + 1 Macc 1:54.
